newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady vs dollar as RBI abstains.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady vs dollar as RBI abstains.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed steady at 35.86/87 against the dollar on Thursday as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) abstained from dollar buying, dealers said.
The dollar was range-bound at 35.860/875 throughout the day.
The rupee eased mildly after an influential Calcutta-based bank bought dollars but quickly stabilised at 35.86/87 after the demand subsided, dealers said.
Forward dollar premiums eased from the opening levels as the expected RBI intervention did not take place, they added.
"The market is heavily over-received," said a dealer, referring to banks which had received premiums against forward dollar sales. Premiums were mostly range-bound.
"Some receivers trickled in seeing that RBI was absent," said a dealer. The six month annualised forward premium closed Thursday steady at 6.92 percent.

"Recent dollar purchases by the RBI at a cost of 7.0 percent run contrary to the market's expectation of further easing of money market rates after the April 15 credit policy," said a foreign bank in a commentary.
"For the moment it is a win-win situation for importers as the rupee remains solid at 35.88 as it has been for the past four months," the bank said.
